value.title: Multiletter Marton achievability
value.objective: Determine whether finite-letter Marton coding can improve half-skew BSSC achievable sum rates and rigorously characterize structural restrictions on candidate multiletter witnesses.

value.title: Conditional-product no-gain structure
value.summary: Characterize conditional-product Marton architectures that cannot yield multiletter gains and develop decomposition-relative correlation tests for remaining coupled candidates.

value.title: Conditional-product Marton no-gain theorem and correlation ledger
value.summary:
Accepted statement:

Let T be any finite receiver-skew two-receiver broadcast channel, and let M_T be its one-letter private-message Marton sum-rate. For every n >= 1, the supremum of the n-letter Marton functional over laws P(w,u^n,v^n,x^n)=P(w) product_i P_i(u_i,v_i,x_i|w), with aggregate U=(U_i) and V=(V_i), equals n M_T. The common W is arbitrary and may correlate coordinates unconditionally. Consequently, any strict two-letter gain for the half-skew BSSC must use a law outside this conditional-product class: every chosen coordinate-packet decomposition under which the factorization could be tested must fail it. For the broader class of arbitrary finite tuple laws P(w,u^n,v^n,x^n), with a chosen aggregate U=(U_i), V=(V_i) and the product channel, the exact total-correlation residual identity in README equation (11) holds, so any strict gain must satisfy the correlation-balance inequality (13) for that decomposition. Trivial constant padding always supplies a tuple representation, but the ledger and its pruning usefulness depend on the noncanonical decomposition. These results do not establish unrestricted Marton additivity, binary-input tightness, a capacity bound, or the exact BSSC capacity.

The equations expressly incorporated by that accepted statement are, for the chosen tuple decomposition,

\[
\begin{aligned}
&L_{1/2,T^{\otimes n}}(P)-\sum_iL_{1/2,T}(P^{(i)})\\
&\quad=\operatorname{TC}(U^n\mid W)+G_{UY}+G_{VZ}-G_{UV}\\
&\qquad\quad-\tfrac12\big[\operatorname{TC}(Y^n\mid W)+\operatorname{TC}(Y^n)+\operatorname{TC}(Z^n\mid W)+\operatorname{TC}(Z^n)\big],
\end{aligned}
\]

and any strict gain forces

\[
\operatorname{TC}(U^n\mid W)+G_{UY}+G_{VZ}-G_{UV}
>\tfrac12\big[\operatorname{TC}(Y^n\mid W)+\operatorname{TC}(Y^n)+\operatorname{TC}(Z^n\mid W)+\operatorname{TC}(Z^n)\big].
\]

Here \(\operatorname{TC}(A^n\mid C)=\sum_iH(A_i\mid C)-H(A^n\mid C)\), \(\operatorname{TC}(A^n)=\sum_iH(A_i)-H(A^n)\), and
\[
\begin{aligned}
G_{UY}&=\sum_iH(Y_i\mid U_i,W)-H(Y^n\mid U^n,W),\\
G_{VZ}&=\sum_iH(Z_i\mid V_i,W)-H(Z^n\mid V^n,W),\\
G_{UV}&=\sum_iH(U_i\mid V_i,W)-H(U^n\mid V^n,W).
\end{aligned}
\]

Scope qualifications (verbatim):
- The theorem applies to finite receiver-skew two-receiver broadcast channels and to the specified conditional-product factorization with a common W that may induce unconditional coordinate correlation.
- A strict-gain law must fail the conditional-product factorization for every exact chosen coordinate-packet decomposition to which the theorem applies.
- For arbitrary tuple laws, the residual ledger and correlation-balance condition are relative to the chosen aggregate coordinate decomposition; they are noncanonical.
- Inequality (13) is only a necessary condition for strict gain, not a sufficient condition.
- Constant padding supplies a tuple representation, but does not make the ledger canonical or necessarily useful for pruning.
- The result does not establish unrestricted Marton additivity, binary-input tightness, a capacity bound, or the exact half-skew BSSC capacity.

value.title: Receiver-skew symmetrization and entropy-ledger proof
value.summary: Proof used to establish the linked accepted claim. Receiver-skew reflection followed by fair-selector symmetrization identifies the one-letter Marton supremum with its midpoint affine functional without assuming attainment. Under the stated conditional-product factorization, the satellite mutual-information terms add exactly coordinatewise, while the common-output terms are subadditive; applying the one-letter bound to each coordinate gives the upper bound n M_T. Independent epsilon-optimal one-letter copies give the reverse inequality. For arbitrary tuple laws over the product channel, direct entropy expansion yields the accepted total-correlation residual identity and makes the stated correlation-balance inequality necessary for any strict gain. This proof item is limited to the linked accepted claim and does not establish unrestricted Marton additivity, binary-input tightness, a capacity bound, or exact BSSC capacity.

placementAudits.rationale: The accepted theorem directly restricts multiletter Marton architectures and supplies a decomposition-relative pruning condition for coupled candidate witnesses, so the existing multiletter Marton achievability program is the narrowest coherent local objective.
